notes.D6: Shared adult/child and bicycle symbols have no dividing line; class-II moped exclusions require a panel.
notes.D7: Vertical division with pedestrians left/cycles right accurately fixes the respective sides.
notes.D8: Blue mounted horse mandates riding path while walking remains permitted; distinct from red C14.
notes.D9: Blue tracked vehicle denotes designated off-road route and permits walking too.
notes.D10: Bus symbol designates scheduled public transport plus legally permitted classes, not all cars.
notes.D11: Crossed bus ends the matching lane designation rather than banning buses.
notes.D12: Orange-plate symbol above left arrow matches this no-letter variant; tunnel-category letters qualify different variants.
notes.E1: Motorway symbol starts its regime unless a distance panel makes it advance information.
notes.E2: Crossed motorway symbol ends motorway or announces distance to end; no unlimited-speed inference.
notes.E3: Front car on green is motortrafikled, distinct from motorway.
notes.E4: Crossed front car ends expressway, subject to any advance distance.
notes.E5: Black skyline starts built-up area; check the applicable signed speed rather than inventing a numeric sign value.
notes.E6: Crossed skyline ends built-up area; other signed limits remain.
notes.E7: Pedestrian-street symbol carries walking pace/yielding and restricted motor-access purposes.
notes.E8: Crossed pedestrians end pedestrian street, without an implied priority entitlement.
notes.E9: Street scene requires walking pace/yielding and restricted parking, not a normal residential-road limit.
notes.E10: Crossed street scene ends the area; exiting does not confer priority.
notes.E11: Blue max 30 km/tim is a recommendation, unlike C31 mandatory limit.
notes.E12: Crossed max 30 ends the recommendation without removing safe-speed duties.
notes.E13: White 50 on black is variable temporary recommended maximum below legal maximum.
notes.E14: White diagonal lines on black end temporary recommendation.
notes.E15: Two red branches merge into one arrow; mutual adaptation rather than priority by force.
notes.E16: Right-pointing horizontal arrow accurately identifies one-way direction.
notes.E17: Red-ended T means no through passage; any bicycle-through variant needs its own symbol.
notes.E18: White M on blue identifies a passing place, not parking.
